questions.stem: Gentle abdominal pressure is painless in a healthy person but very painful over an inflamed appendix. Which mechanism explains this tenderness?

options.A: Referred pain via convergent spinal neurons
options.B: Lowered nociceptor threshold from inflammatory mediators
options.D: Neuropathic pain from direct nerve injury
options.E: Exaggeration by the emotional component of pain

questions.explanation: Sensitization: bradykinin, prostaglandins, leukotrienes and substance P lower the activation threshold of pain pathways; this is the basis of clinical tenderness. A: Referred pain is felt away from the source. C: Opioid circuits diminish pain. D: The nerve itself isn't the source. E: The emotional component varies perception but doesn't explain localized tenderness over inflamed tissue.

questions.stem: Impulses from a stimulated nociceptor spread into neighboring terminal branches and release a peptide that causes vasodilation, neurogenic edema, and mast-cell histamine release. Which peptide?
questions.explanation: Substance P mediates secondary activation: vasodilation, neurogenic edema, histamine from mast cells and serotonin from platelets. A: Bradykinin is produced in damaged tissue, not released from nerve terminals. B: Prostaglandins sensitize terminals but aren't peptides. C: Serotonin is released from platelets in response to substance P. E: β-endorphin is an endogenous opioid that reduces pain.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old woman has severe burning pain along a thoracic dermatome 2 months after a vesicular rash resolved. Light clothing brushing the skin is excruciating. What is this phenomenon?
questions.explanation: After herpes zoster the nerve itself is the source (neuropathic), and very light moving stimuli become painful (allodynia). A: Pain is in the involved dermatome, not referred. B: The inflammation has resolved. D: Not a placebo effect. E: This is somatic and dermatomal, not visceral.

questions.stem: A patient reports less pain after an inert pill he was told is a strong analgesic. Which system most likely mediates this?
questions.explanation: Suggestion and reassurance act through pain-modulation circuits; the pain-diminishing ones use endogenous opioids (the basis of the placebo effect). A: Sensitization increases pain. B: Substance P amplifies pain. C: Prostaglandins sensitize nociceptors. D: Bradykinin causes pain.

questions.stem: A patient with irritation of the diaphragm complains of shoulder pain. What explains this?

options.A: Fibers from both sites converge on a common spinal cell body
options.C: The phrenic nerve itself is the source of the pain
options.D: The organ activates the same CNS cells as its overlying skin

questions.explanation: Referred pain: pain fibers from different locations converge on the same spinal cell, so the brain misattributes the source. B: There is no shoulder pathology to sensitize. C: Neuropathic pain arises from a damaged nerve, not irritation of an organ. D: That is the normal mechanism that localizes deep pain correctly to the overlying skin, not to a distant site. E: Modulation changes intensity, not location.
